rule.body: For "nearest in meaning", read the whole sentence first and work out what the underlined word must mean there. Then put each option in its place: the right one keeps the meaning of the sentence the same. Watch out for opposites and for words that merely sound related.
rule.example: "The [[obsolete]] machine was thrown away": try "outdated" in its place, and the meaning stays the same.

questions.stem: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: The instructions were so [[ambiguous]] that half the class answered the wrong question.
questions.explanation: "Ambiguous" means open to more than one meaning, that is, unclear. That is why students misread the question.

questions.stem: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: After the long journey, Musa felt so [[lethargic]] that he slept through the afternoon.
questions.explanation: "Lethargic" means tired and lacking energy, which is what "sluggish" means.

questions.stem: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: Typewriters have become [[obsolete]] in most offices since computers arrived.
questions.explanation: "Obsolete" means no longer in use because something newer has replaced it, that is, outdated.

questions.stem: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: Mrs Eze is a [[meticulous]] accountant who checks every figure twice.
questions.explanation: "Meticulous" means paying close attention to every detail, that is, very careful.

questions.stem: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: Bisi is [[frugal]]; she buys only what she needs and saves the rest of her allowance.
questions.explanation: "Frugal" means careful not to waste money, which is what "thrifty" means.

questions.stem: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: Although Chidi was usually [[reticent]], he spoke at length during the debate.
questions.explanation: "Reticent" means quiet and slow to share one's thoughts, that is, reserved. "Although" shows it contrasts with speaking at length.

questions.stem: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: The chief's [[ostentatious]] party, with gold-plated cups and three live bands, was the talk of the town.
questions.explanation: "Ostentatious" describes a display meant to impress people with wealth, that is, showy.

questions.stem: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: Despite failing twice, Ngozi remained [[tenacious]] and passed the exam on her third attempt.
questions.explanation: "Tenacious" means refusing to give up, which is what "persistent" means.

questions.stem: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: The journalist was [[candid]] about her mistakes, admitting every one of them in public.
questions.explanation: "Candid" means honest and open, even about uncomfortable things, that is, frank.

questions.stem: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: The court's ruling [[vindicated]] the teacher, who had been wrongly accused of theft.
questions.explanation: To "vindicate" someone is to show they were right or innocent, that is, to clear them of blame.
